build_cmd: dune build @install  (run inside solvers/alt-ergo with its local opam switch active: eval $(opam env --switch=. --set-switch))
solved_condition: A query counts as solved when Alt-Ergo answers `unsat` within the time limit. Alt-Ergo produces no proofs, so there is no proof check — the soundness canaries (satisfiable queries that must never be answered `unsat`) are what keep it honest. The query is first rewritten from z3-dialect to standard SMT-LIB by `scripts/prep_smtlib.py` (part of the frozen referee); the solver sees that rewritten input.
metric: mean gap to Z3 in percentage points over the four sets (lower is better; 0 = as good as Z3)

anchors.zero: the unmodified solver at solver_base_commit (the starting point)
anchors.one: Z3 with the verifier's options (the reference; its internals are not provided)

baseline.note: on the --sample 20 dev split (~2 queries per set); sample-sensitive, directional only. Re-measure with a larger sample or --split full for a stable baseline.

license_note: The config.env default ALTERGO_REF=next is under the OCamlPro Non-Commercial License. Use ALTERGO_REF=v2.4.3-free (CeCILL-C, the paper's version) for open/commercial use; that release needs scripts/prep_smtlib.py --legacy-ae.
